text: Never run `terraform apply` locally against prod. Open a PR; plan.yml posts the plan and apply runs from CI after approval.
Each environment has its own root in envs/<env>/. Run `terraform -chdir=envs/staging plan`; there is no root module at the repo top.
An RDS major upgrade needs a new parameter group with the new family (postgres16). The old group can't be reused and the apply fails late.
Set allow_major_version_upgrade = true only in the upgrade PR, then turn it off again; left on, a stray engine_version bump can upgrade prod.
Prod database changes need a fresh manual snapshot and a maintenance window announced in #ops-changes 48 hours ahead.
Use RDS blue/green deployments for prod major upgrades; the in-place upgrade on staging caused about 25 minutes of downtime.
Before a PR: `make fmt validate lint` (terraform fmt, validate, tflint) plus checkov. CI blocks on any failure.
Every new module input goes in variables.tf with a type and description; then regenerate the module README with `terraform-docs .`.
Prod RDS stays on Postgres 13 until the vendor extension supports newer versions.
State lives in local terraform.tfstate files committed to the repo.
Remote state is S3 with DynamoDB locking, one state per env. Use `terraform force-unlock` only after checking that no CI run holds the lock.
The EKS module pins the VPC CNI add-on version; upgrade add-ons one minor version at a time.
CloudFront distributions for the marketing site live in envs/global/cdn.tf and are owned by the web team.
GitHub OIDC roles are in modules/github-oidc; trust is per branch, so a new deploy branch needs a trust-policy update.
Change one environment per PR: staging changes merge and soak for a day before the prod PR is opened.
S3 buckets need a public access block and default encryption; checkov CKV_AWS_18 (access logging) is waived only for the logs bucket.
Terraform is pinned in .terraform-version (1.9.x) via tfenv; provider versions are pinned in each module's versions.tf.
Every resource needs team and cost_center tags, set through default_tags in the provider block.
Session Redis (ElastiCache) is defined in envs/prod/cache.tf; failover is tested every quarter.
Use parameter_group_name = "default.postgres13" on aws_db_instance; custom parameter groups aren't needed.
After a Postgres major upgrade, run ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE for pg_stat_statements and postgis on each database.
Route53 records for customer custom domains are managed by the domains service through the API, not Terraform; don't import them.
